Spread over {{convert|16|sqkm}}, it is located about {{convert|35|km||abbr=on}} north of the city, near the suburb of [[Devanahalli]]. It is owned and operated by Bengaluru International Airport Limited (BIAL), a [[public–private partnership|public–private consortium]]. The airport opened in May 2008, as an alternative to the increasingly congested [[HAL Airport]], the original commercial airport serving the city. It is named after [[Kempe Gowda I]], the founder of Bengaluru. It is Karnataka's first fully [[solar power]]ed airport, developed by CleanMax Solar.{{cite news |title=CleanMax Solar to power Chennai Metro – Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/cleanmax-solar-to-power-chennai-metro/articleshow/59285311.cms |work=The Times of India |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170927041952/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/cleanmax-solar-to-power-chennai-metro/articleshow/59285311.cms |archive-date=27 September 2017}}{{cite web |title=Kempegowda International Airport |url=https://cleanmaxsolar.com/pdf/BIAL-case-study.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922194708/https://cleanmaxsolar.com/pdf/BIAL-case-study.pdf |archive-date=22 September 2017 |access-date=19 September 2017}} The airport is the [[List of the busiest airports in India|third-busiest in India]],{{cite web |title=Busiest Airports in India: Passenger Traffic Rankings (2026) |work=Just Aviation |date=18 May 2025 |url=https://justaviation.aero/busiest-airports-in-india/ |access-date=19 July 2026 }} behind the airports in [[Indira Gandhi International Airport|Delhi]] and [[Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport|Mumbai]]. It is the [[List of the busiest airports in Asia|26th busiest airport in Asia]] and the 54th busiest airport in the world as of 2024.{{cite web |url=https://www.panynj.gov/content/dam/airports/statistics/statistics-general-info/annual-atr/ATR_2023.pdf |title=2023 Airport Traffic Report |work=Port Authority of New York and New Jersey |date=April 2024 |page=32}} In FY2025-26, the airport handled over 44.47 million passengers and {{convert|532012|t|ST}} of cargo.{{cite web|title=Annexure III – Passenger Data|url=https://www.aai.aero/sites/default/files/traffic-news/Mar2k26Annex3.pdf|website=aai.aero|access-date=24 May 2026}}{{cite web |title=Annexure IV – Freight Movement Data |url=https://www.aai.aero/sites/default/files/traffic-news/Mar2k26Annex4.pdf |website=aai.aero |access-date=24 May 2026}} The airport offers connecting flights to all 6 inhabited continents, and direct flights to 5. The airport has two passenger terminals that handle both domestic and international operations, and two runways, the second of which was commissioned on 6 December 2019.{{cite news |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/airlines-/-aviation/lt-bags-bengaluru-airport-contract-to-build-terminal-two/articleshow/66054706.cms |newspaper=Economic Times |title=L&T bags Bengaluru airport contract to build terminal two |date=3 October 2018 |access-date=7 August 2019}}{{cite news |title=First flight takes off from second runway at Bengaluru airport |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/first-flight-takes-off-from-second-runway-at-bengaluru-airport/article30219423.ece |access-date=9 December 2019 |work=The Hindu |date=6 December 2019 |language=en-IN |archive-date=9 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191209170431/https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/first-flight-takes-off-from-second-runway-at-bengaluru-airport/article30219423.ece |url-status=live}} The second terminal was inaugurated by [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] on 11 November 2022.{{cite news |title=PM inaugurates swanky Terminal-2 of Bengaluru airport |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/bengaluru/2022/Nov/11/pm-inaugurates-swanky-terminal-2-of-bengaluru-airport-2517262.html |work=The New Indian Express |date=11 November 2022 |access-date=13 November 2022 |language=en}}{{cite news |title=All international flights from Bengaluru airport will move to Terminal 2 from September 1 |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/all-intl-flights-from-kia-will-move-to-t2-from-september-1/articleshow/100861031.cms |work=The Times of India |date=9 June 2023 |access-date=13 June 2023 |language=en}} There is also a cargo village with 3 cargo terminals. The airport serves a hub for [[Air India]], [[Alliance Air (India)|Alliance Air]], [[DHL Aviation]], [[FedEx Express]] and [[Star Air (India)|Star Air]],{{cite web |url=https://enmobile.prnasia.com/releases/apac/dhl-express-opens-its-eur22-million-expanded-bengaluru-gateway-to-support-e-commerce-growth-338361.shtml |title=DHL Express opens its EUR22 million expanded Bengaluru Gateway to support e-commerce growth |access-date=1 February 2022 |website=enmobile.prnasia.com}} as well as an operating base for [[Air India Express]], [[Akasa Air]] and [[IndiGo]]. == History == === Planning (1991–2004) === The original airport serving Bengaluru was [[HAL Airport]], located {{convert|5|km}} from the city centre. It was the primary airport in the city until 2008. Originally established in 1942 for military and defence purposes, HAL began domestic operations for the first time in the late 1970s. The unexpected popularity of newly offered domestic flights encouraged rapid expansion of the airport. In the late 1990s, the first international services began, with [[Air India]] flights to [[Changi Airport|Singapore]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bangalore-blr.airports-guides.com/blr_history.html Karnataka]] decided to call for international consortia to own, build and operate the new [[greenfield airport]].{{cite news |title=Realising the new Bangalore Airport |url=https://www.internationalairportreview.com/article/1361/realising-the-new-bangalore-airport/ |access-date=23 February 2025 |work=International Airport Review |date=28 September 2007}} In December 1995, a consortium made up of the [[Tata Group]], [[Raytheon]] and [[Singapore Changi Airport]] signed a [[memorandum of understanding|memorandum of understanding (MoU)]] with the State Government regarding participation in the project. In June 1998, however, the consortium announced it was pulling out of the project due to delays in government approval. These included disputes over the location of the new airport and the fate of HAL Airport.{{cite news |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/economy/story/19980727-tripped-by-politics-tata-group-airline-project-falls-apart-826792-1998-07-19 |title=This flight is delayed |last=Chakravarti |first=Sudeep |date=20 July 1998 |work=[[India Today]] |access-date=30 March 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403154129/http://indiatoday.intoday.in/story/tripped-by-politics-tata-group-airline-project-falls-apart/1/264643.html |archive-date=3 April 2016}} In May 1999, the [[Airports Authority of India]] (AAI) and the Karnataka State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (KSIIDC) signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) regarding the project. It would be a [[public–private partnership]], with AAI and KSIIDC holding a 26% share and private companies holding the remaining 74%. In January 2001, the State Government created the company Bengaluru International Airport Limited (BIAL) as a [[special purpose entity]], and began searching for partners.{{cite news |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2001/01/10/stories/1410043z.htm |title=Hunt for Devanahalli airport partners begins |last=D. S. |first=Madhumathi |date=9 January 2001 |newspaper=[[The Hindu Business Line]] |access-date=9 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403154257/http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2001/01/10/stories/1410043z.htm |archive-date=3 April 2016}} By November, the project had attracted [[Zurich Airport (company)|Zürich Airport]], [[Siemens Project Ventures]] and [[Larsen & Toubro]].{{cite news |url=http://www.rediff.com/money/2001/nov/01siemen.htm |title=Siemens team wins bid to build international airport in Bangalore: Reuters |date=1 November 2001 |work=[[Rediff]] |access-date=22 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024213153/http://www.rediff.com/money/2001/nov/01siemen.htm |archive-date=24 October 2012}} Construction was expected to begin in October 2002;{{cite news |url=http://www.thehindu.com/2005/05/07/stories/2005050709660500.htm |title=Devanahalli airport work has begun |date=7 May 2005 |newspaper=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=9 March 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403154427/http://www.thehindu.com/2005/05/07/stories/2005050709660500.htm |archive-date=3 April 2016}} however, governmental delays persisted.{{cite news |url=http://www.livemint.com/Opinion/UlZNfeC5zHuAMc2rWN3eIK/Grounded-at-the-word-go.html |title=Grounded at the word go |last=Ramanathan |first=Ramesh |date=11 February 2008 |newspaper=[[Live Mint]] |access-date=9 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310220155/http://www.livemint.com/Opinion/UlZNfeC5zHuAMc2rWN3eIK/Grounded-at-the-word-go.html |archive-date=10 March 2016}}{{cite news |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2004/03/19/stories/2004031901131700.htm |title=Ministry clears Bangalore airport project – BIAL seeks review of draft version of concession pact |last=D. S. |first=Madhumathi |date=18 March 2004 |newspaper=[[The Hindu Business Line]] |access-date=9 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050913114523/http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2004/03/19/stories/2004031901131700.htm |archive-date=13 September 2005}} The [[Union Council of Ministers|Union Cabinet]] approved the project in February 2000.{{cite news |title=Cabinet nod for Devanahalli airport project |url=http://www.deccanherald.com/deccanherald/feb02/nod.htm |access-date=5 May 2024 |work=Deccan Herald |date=2 February 2000 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000302181644/http://www.deccanherald.com/deccanherald/feb02/nod.htm |archive-date=2 March 2000}} The [[concession (contract)|concession agreement]] between the State Government, the Union Government and BIAL was signed in July 2004, and it required the closure of HAL Airport.{{cite news |date=5 July 2004 |title=Concession agreement for airport signed |url=http://www.thehindu.com/2004/07/06/stories/2004070606800600.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050216222735/http://www.thehindu.com/2004/07/06/stories/2004070606800600.htm |archive-date=16 February 2005 |access-date=9 March 2016 |newspaper=[[The Hindu]]}}{{cite news |url=http://www.thehindu.com/2004/06/16/stories/2004061615330100.htm |title=All clear now for new Bangalore airport |date=15 June 2004 |newspaper=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=30 March 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403154641/http://www.thehindu.com/2004/06/16/stories/2004061615330100.htm |archive-date=3 April 2016}} It took nearly a decade to progress from the initial stages of land allocation and acquisition, to the signing of shareholder agreements in 2002 and the start of construction. === Design === When the project was initiated, BIAL anticipated traffic of approximately 5 million passengers per annum in the first few years of operations. However, the scale of air traffic growth in the city meant that the figure was already breached by 2008. It took more than 9 months to redesign the project and gain permission for expansion. By the time the approvals for the reworked project were sanctioned, construction was half completed. Despite the challenges, BIAL expected the airport to be operational by the initially proposed date of completion. The revised increase in capacity catered to 11 million passengers per annum, more than doubling the previous estimates. BIAL's modified plan was to build a terminal with 8 [[Jet bridge|passenger boarding bridges]], 1 double arm aerobridge, 9 remote bus gates and a single, {{convert|4000|m|adj=on}} long runway. BIAL also planned to build an apron with 42 Code-C aircraft stands (with 8 contact stands), as well as an air and land-side road system. The estimated cost for the entire project at the time was {{INRConvert|1930|c}}. === Construction and opening (2005–2008) === Construction commenced on 2 July 2005, and was completed in 32 months. BIAL set the launch date for 30 March 2008.{{cite news |date=27 June 2005 |title=Bangalore airport work to begin on July 2 |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/tp-logistics/bangalore-airport-work-to-begin-on-july-2/article2181575.ece |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403154706/http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/tp-logistics/bangalore-airport-work-to-begin-on-july-2/article2181575.ece |archive-date=3 April 2016 |access-date=9 March 2016 |newspaper=[[The Hindu Business Line]]}}{{cite news |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/tp-logistics/bangalore-international-airport-launch-set-for-march-30/article1672728.ece |title=Bangalore international airport launch set for March 30 |last=D. In March 2008, AAI employees initiated a massive strike against the closure of HAL Airport in Bengaluru and [[Begumpet Airport]] in Hyderabad, fearing they would lose their jobs.{{cite news |url=http://gulfnews.com/news/asia/india/slow-take-off-for-airport-stir-1.91196 |title=Slow take-off for airport stir |date=13 March 2008 |work=Gulf News |access-date=30 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304105007/http://gulfnews.com/news/asia/india/slow-take-off-for-airport-stir-1.91196 |archive-date=4 March 2016}} The Bangalore City Connect Foundation, a group of citizens and businessmen, staged a rally in mid-May, claiming the new airport was too small for the latest demand projections.{{cite news |url=http://www.livemint.com/Politics/jMGy6T5cnMis3F87KFkqOM/Citizen8217s-body-protests-closure-of-old-Bangalore-airpo.html |title=Citizen's body protests closure of old Bangalore airport |last=Raghu |first=K. |date=17 May 2008 |newspaper=[[Live Mint]] |access-date=30 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403155052/http://www.livemint.com/Politics/jMGy6T5cnMis3F87KFkqOM/Citizen8217s-body-protests-closure-of-old-Bangalore-airpo.html |archive-date=3 April 2016}}{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/7405287.stm |title=Battle over new Bangalore airport |last=Vaswani |first=Karishma |date=16 May 2008 |work=[[BBC News]] |access-date=30 March 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080521042652/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/7405287.stm |archive-date=21 May 2008}} On 23 May, a hearing was held at the [[Karnataka High Court]] over poor connectivity between the city and the airport. March 2016}} The construction of the second runway (09R/27L) at the airport was completed and the runway inaugurated on 6 December 2019, with the departure of [[IndiGo]] Flight 466 (6E466) to [[Rajiv Gandhi International Airport|Hyderabad]].{{cite web |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/state/top-karnataka-stories/first-flight-takes-off-from-second-runway-of-kia-783345.html |title=First flight takes off from second runway of KIA |date=6 December 2019 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en |access-date=14 December 2019 |archive-date=7 December 2019 It is equipped with [[Category III approach|CAT IIIB ILS]]. The runway also features a parallel taxiway and two cross-field taxiways in the east, linking the new runway to the old runway and the aprons at Terminal 1 and Terminal 2. The original runway (09L/27R) was also upgraded as part of the expansion work.{{cite web |title=KIA begins work on 2nd runway; to be linked to Terminal 2 apron |url=http://www.deccanherald.com/content/578752/kia-begins-work-2nd-runway.html |website=Deccan Herald |access-date=17 March 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118161410/http://www.deccanherald.com/content/578752/kia-begins-work-2nd-runway.html |archive-date=18 January 2017 |date=November 2016}} The old runway (09L/27R) was closed from 22 June 2020 for nine months for rehabilitation and strengthening.{{Cite news |title=Closed Kempegowda International Airport runway to begin operations by March-end |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/bengaluru/2021/feb/08/closed-kempegowda-international-airport-runway-to-begin-operations-by-march-end-2261000.html |access-date=6 April 2021 |work=The New Indian Express |date=8 February 2021 |archive-date=25 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225093105/https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/bengaluru/2021/feb/08/closed-kempegowda-international-airport-runway-to-begin-operations-by-march-end-2261000.html |url-status=live}} It was opened for operations again on 31 March 2021, along with the operational south runway. On doing so, KIA became the first airport in [[South India]] to facilitate parallel runway operations.{{Cite news |date=26 March 2021 |title=Bengaluru: Kempegowda International Airport gets parallel runways, first in south India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/bengaluru-kempegowda-international-airport-gets-parallel-runways-first-in-south-india/articleshow/81698799.cms |access-date=6 April 2021 |work=The Times of India |language=en |archive-date=27 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210327095251/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/bengaluru-kempegowda-international-airport-gets-parallel-runways-first-in-south-india/articleshow/81698799.cms |url-status=live}} The north runway (09L/27R) is approved for and capable of low-visibility takeoffs, allowing aircraft movement even when the runway visual range (RVR) is as low as 125m. Civil works to also equip this runway with a [[Category III approach|CAT IIIB ILS]] system were completed in December 2024.{{cite news |last1=Mathew Philip |first1=Christin |date=4 October 2024 |title=Bengaluru airport's elevated taxiway work to commence in Q1 2025: BIAL |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/india/bengaluru-airports-elevated-taxiway-work-to-commence-in-q1-2025-bial-12835684.html |work=MoneyControl |access-date=5 October 2024}} The calibration for the [[Instrument landing system|ILS]] was completed in January 2025 and full [[Category III approach|CAT IIIB ILS]] capability was made operational in May 2025.{{cite news |last1=S |first1=Lalitha |date=11 January 2025 |title=AAI successfully calibrates ILS on KIA's north runway, set for full operation by May 2025 |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/bengaluru/2025/Jan/11/aai-successfully-calibrates-ils-on-kias-north-runway-set-for-full-operation-by-may-2025 |work=The New Indian Express |access-date=11 January 2025}} With runway upgrades on the Northern runway completed, both runways and associated taxiways are capable of handling Code-F aircraft such as the [[Airbus A380]] and [[Boeing 747-8]].{{cite news |last1=C S |first1=Hemanth |date=5 September 2025 |title=Both runways at KIA Bengaluru can now handle Airbus A380 aircraft |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/both-runways-of-kia-now-compatible-for-wide-bodied-aircraft-operations/article70012737.ece |work=The Hindu |access-date=16 September 2025}} === Terminals === ====Terminal 1==== {{multiple image | width = 150 | perrow = 2 | image1 = Terminal 1 of Kempegowda International Airport.jpg | image2 = Bengaluru Airport International Departures.jpg | footer = ''(Left)'': Front view of Terminal 1; ''(Right)'': Erstwhile international departures section at Terminal 1 | alt1 = sdas | total_width = 350 }} The original terminal building can handle 35 million passengers per annum, and handles all domestic flights operated by [[IndiGo]], [[Akasa Air]], [[Alliance Air (India)|Alliance Air]] and [[SpiceJet]]. Check-in and baggage reclaim is situated on the lower floor, while departure gates are located on the lower & upper floors. Boarding gates 1&2, 12–18 and 28–43 on the upper floor are equipped with jet bridges. Boarding gates 3–9 and 19–25 on the lower floor form the Western and Eastern bus gates respectively.{{cite web |url=https://www.bengaluruairport.com/map |title=Terminal Maps |work=Kempegowda International Airport Bengaluru}} Gates 41–42 are equipped to serve the world's largest passenger aircraft, the [[Airbus A380]].{{cite news |url=http://www.ndtv.com/bangalore-news/bangalore-airport-named-after-city-founder-kempegowda-544566 |title=Bangalore airport named after city founder Kempegowda |date=15 December 2013 |work=[[NDTV]] |access-date=15 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160319002923/http://www.ndtv.com/bangalore-news/bangalore-airport-named-after-city-founder-kempegowda-544566 |archive-date=19 March 2016}} Since 12 September 2023, with the shift of all international flights to Terminal 2, Terminal 1 has become a domestic-only operation.{{cite news |date=10 September 2023 |title=KIA's Terminal-2 will handle both international and domestic flights |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/kias-terminal-2-will-handle-both-international-and-domestic-flights/article67292029.ece |access-date=12 September 2023 |website=[[The Hindu]]}} In 2019, BIAL retracted the rights of Above Ground Level and Plaza Premium to operate the lounges in Terminal 1, and decided to operate them by themselves. Following this decision, and the transfer of international flights, there are now only two lounges in Terminal 1: the BLR Domestic Lounge and the new 080 Domestic Lounge (which is split into 2 disconnected lounges, as 1 used to serve the erstwhile international departures).{{Cite web |title=BLR Airport Lounge Guide: Kempegowda International |url=https://www.loungepair.com/blog/airport-lounge-guide-kempegowda-international-airport-bengaluru |access-date=29 December 2024 |website=LoungePair |language=en-NZ}} Named "080" after the trunk dial code of the city, the new lounge aims to pay an ode to the culture of Bengaluru with local artistry, regional culture-inspired interiors and botanical elements. Both lounges are operated by Travel Food Services on behalf of the airport.{{cite web |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/bangalore/bengaluru-airport-080-lounge-terminal-one-7959508/ |title=Bengaluru airport unveils '080 Lounge' at terminal one |date=9 June 2022 |access-date=15 September 2022}} ====Terminal 2==== {{multiple image | width = 150 | perrow = 2 | image1 = Terminal 2 Departure of Kempegowda International Airport.jpg | image2 = BLRT2 IntlDep.jpg | footer = ''(Left)'': Front view of Terminal 2; ''(Right)'': International departures area at Terminal 2 | alt1 = sdas | total_width = 350 }} The airport's second terminal was designed as a tribute to the 'Garden City' title of [[Bengaluru]] by [[Skidmore, Owings & Merrill]], and was constructed by [[Larsen & Toubro]]. Construction of the first phase commenced in 2018, but the project faced delays owing to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |date=17 September 2021 |title=Pandemic delays completion of Bengaluru airport's Terminal II |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/bangalore/pandemic-delays-completion-of-bengaluru-airports-terminal-ii-7514695/ |access-date=10 November 2022 |website=The Indian Express |language=en-US}} It was inaugurated on 11 November 2022 by [[Narendra Modi|Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi]], and began operations in January 2023. The first phase of Terminal 2, built at a cost of {{INRConvert|5000|c}}, is {{convert|255000|m2}} and will help augment the capacity of the airport by an additional 25 million passengers per annum.{{cite web |title=Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport gets SWANKY new Terminal 2: All you need to KNOW - Design, Features, Capacity |url=https://zeenews.india.com/aviation/bengalurus-kempegowda-international-airport-gets-swanky-new-terminal-2-all-you-need-to-know-design-features-capacity-2533361.html |access-date=10 November 2022 |website=Zee News |language=en-US}} The second phase of Terminal 2 is under construction to increase capacity by an additional 20 million passengers per annum.{{cite web |title=KIA's garden-themed Terminal-2 massive in size |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/content/653955/kias-garden-themed-terminal-2.html |access-date=10 November 2022 |website=Deccan Herald |date=15 January 2018 |language=en-US}} Arrivals are situated on the ground floor, while departures are on the first floor. The first phase of Terminal 2 features 95 check-in counters, 17 security lanes, 9 baggage claim belts, 34 conventional and 6 electronic immigration gates. With provisions for Code-F gates to handle larger aircraft like the [[Airbus A380]] and the [[Boeing 747-8]], the first phase of Terminal 2 began domestic operations on 15 January 2023, with [[Star Air (India)|Star Air]] Flight 117 (S5117) to [[Kalaburagi Airport|Kalaburagi]] being the first scheduled flight to use the new terminal.{{cite web |title=Bengaluru airport's Terminal 2 to begin domestic operations on January 15 |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/bangalore/bengaluru-airport-terminal-2-begin-domestic-operations-on-january-15-8373826/ |access-date=11 January 2023 |website=Indian Express |date=10 January 2023 |language=en-US}} On 12 September 2023, Terminal 2 began handling all international operations, with [[Saudia]] Flight 867 (SV867) from [[King Abdulaziz International Airport|Jeddah]] operating the first international arrival and subsequent departure.{{cite web |title=International flight operations to commence from Terminal 2 of Bengaluru airport Tuesday |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/bangalore/bengaluru-airport-terminal-2-international-flight-operations-8935449/ |access-date=12 September 2023 |website=Indian Express |date=11 September 2023 |language=en-US}} In addition to handling all international operations, Terminal 2 also handles all domestic flights operated by [[Air India]], [[Air India Express]] and [[Star Air (India)|Star Air]]. === Aviation fuel services === The airport has a fuel farm spread over {{convert|11|acre}}, west of the cargo village and passenger terminal. It was built by [[Indian Oil|Indian Oil Skytanking Ltd (IOSL)]], but is shared by multiple oil companies.{{cite news |url=http://www.rediff.com/money/2008/aug/19oil.htm |title=Fuel deals: Indian Oil JV eyes Mumbai, Delhi airports |last=Kulkarni |first=Mahesh |date=19 August 2008 |work=[[Rediff]] |access-date=12 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110415173317/http://www.rediff.com/money/2008/aug/19oil.htm |archive-date=15 April 2011}} In October 2008, [[Indian Oil Corporation|IndianOil]] commissioned a {{convert|36|km|mi|adj=on}} fuel [[pipeline transport|pipeline]] between its storage terminal in Devanagonthi and Kempegowda International Airport.{{cite news |url=https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-karnataka/IOC-does-its-groundwork-for-Devanahalli-airport/article15322699.ece |title=IOC does its groundwork for Devanahalli airport |date=15 October 2008 |newspaper=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=12 March 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403162339/http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-karnataka/ioc-does-its-groundwork-for-devanahalli-airport/article1357276.ece |archive-date=3 April 2016}} === Cargo facilities === The airport has 3 cargo terminals. One is operated by AISATS Ltd. (Air India Singapore Airport Terminal Services Limited) and includes a facility for storing [[pharmaceutical drug|pharmaceuticals]].{{cite news |url=http://aircargoworld.com/menzies-opens-pharma-cold-zone-in-bangalore-9993/ |title=Menzies opens pharma cold zone in Bangalore |date=25 August 2014 |work=Air Cargo World |access-date=12 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150326025459/http://aircargoworld.com/menzies-opens-pharma-cold-zone-in-bangalore-9993/ |archive-date=26 March 2015}} [[DHL Aviation|DHL]] and [[Blue Dart Aviation]] jointly operate a {{convert|221000|ft2|m2|order=flip|adj=on|}} terminal.{{cite news |url=http://www.bangaloreaviation.com/2008/11/dhl-and-blue-dart-open-integrated.html |title=DHL and Blue Dart open integrated terminal at Bangalore airport |last=Agarwal |first=Devesh |date=21 November 2008 |work=Bangalore Aviation |access-date=31 March 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160412203947/http://www.bangaloreaviation.com/2008/11/dhl-and-blue-dart-open-integrated.html |archive-date=12 April 2016}} The third cargo terminal is operated by Menzies Aviation Bobba (Bangalore) Pvt. Ltd, a joint venture between [[Menzies Aviation]] and Bobba Group (a sales agency for [[Lufthansa Cargo]]). The {{convert|170000|ft2|m2|order=flip|adj=on|}} cargo terminal began operations in May 2008. Additionally, a greenfield domestic cargo terminal spanning {{convert|305000|ft2|m2|order=flip|adj=on|}} opened in February 2025.{{Cite web |date=28 February 2025 |title=Bengaluru airport gets country's largest greenfield domestic cargo terminal, new facility spread over 7 acres |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/bangalore/bengaluru-airport-greenfield-domestic-cargo-terminal-facility-9860260/ |access-date=2 March 2025 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} Combined, the terminal has the capacity to handle {{convert|680000|t|ST}} tons of cargo annually.{{cite news |url=https://www.menziesbobba.com/cargo.php |title=Mezies Aviation Cargo |access-date=23 November 2022 |archive-date=1 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201200932/https://menziesbobba.com/cargo.php |url-status=dead }} Altogether, the airport has the capacity to process up to {{convert|1400000|t|ST}} of cargo annually and currently sees ~{{convert|450000|t|ST}} handled per year.{{Cite web |date=16 April 2024 |title=Bengaluru Airport cargo handled up 7% in FY2024 |url=https://www.itln.in/aviation/bengaluru-airport-cargo-handled-up-7-in-fy2024-1351865 |access-date=29 December 2024 |website=www.itln.in |language=en}} The airport processes the highest amount of [[Shelf life|perishable]] cargo in the country.{{Cite news |date=4 July 2024 |title=Bengaluru airport tops in perishable exports from India for fourth year |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/airlines-/-aviation/bengaluru-airport-tops-in-perishable-exports-from-india-for-fourth-year/articleshow/111488708.cms?from=mdr#:~:text=Bengaluru's%20Kempegowda%20International%20Airport%20remains,share%20for%20FY%202023-24. |access-date=29 December 2024 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} BIAL inaugurated a separate cargo village in December 2008. The village is spread over {{convert|11|acre}} and includes office spaces, conference rooms, a cafeteria for staff and parking space for nearly 80 trucks.{{cite news |date=10 December 2008 |title=Cargo village takes off at B'lore airport |url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/cargo-village-takes-off-at-b-39-lore-airport-108121001006_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403162431/http://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/cargo-village-takes-off-at-b-39-lore-airport-108121001006_1.html |archive-date=3 April 2016 |access-date=31 March 2016 |newspaper=[[Business Standard]]}} ===Other facilities=== ====IndiGo iFly Training Academy==== On 4 September 2019, India's biggest airline [[IndiGo]] announced that it would extend its learning academy, iFly, to Bengaluru, its 2nd such facility in the country.{{Cite news |date=4 September 2019 |title=IndiGo launches 2nd ifly facility in Bengaluru |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/airlines-/-aviation/indigo-launches-2nd-ifly-facility-in-bengaluru/articleshow/70976545.cms?from=mdr |access-date=1 January 2025 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} From 6 September 2019 onwards, iFly began facilitating training to IndiGo flight crew. With over 27,000 employees, there are over 100 instructors in the academy who conduct workshops and training exercises on a regular basis.{{cite web |date=4 September 2019 |title=IndiGo launches second iFLY facility in Bengaluru |url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/business/news-bengaluru-indigo-launches-second-ifly-facility-547238 |access-date=26 February 2022}} ====Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul Facilities==== [[IndiGo]]'s second MRO facility to service their fleet of [[Airbus]] jets is located at KIA. The {{convert|218000|ft2|m2|order=flip|adj=on|}} facility has capacity for narrow-body aircraft and houses a single bay catering for widebody aircraft.{{cite web |url=https://aviationweek.com/mro/services-support/indigo-expands-maintenance-capabilities-bangalore |title=IndiGo Expands Maintenance Capabilities To Bangalore |date=26 July 2022 |access-date=15 September 2022}} The MRO became operational in November 2022.{{cite news |title=IndiGo inaugurates second MRO facility at Bengaluru airport |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/airlines-/-aviation/indigo-inaugurates-second-mro-facility-at-bengaluru-airport/articleshow/95707291.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=23 November 2022 |access-date=25 November 2022 |language=en}} As of May 2025, IndiGo is currently in the process of constructing a second MRO of roughly {{convert|1400000|ft2|m2|order=flip|adj=on|}} at the airport, in order to service wide-body aircraft.{{Cite news |date=30 May 2025 |title=IndiGo to build another MRO facility at Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/indigo-to-build-another-mro-facility-at-kempegowda-international-airport-in-bengaluru/article69636931.ece |access-date=2 August 2025 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} Aligning with their vision to establish a hub at the airport, [[Air India]] signed a [[Memorandum of understanding|memorandum of understanding (MoU)]] in February 2024 to build Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) facilities at Kempegowda International Airport, for airframe maintenance of both [[Wide-body aircraft|wide-body]] and [[Narrow-body aircraft|narrow-body]] jets, including heavy structural checks.{{cite news |title=Air India and Tata Advanced Systems sign an MOU with Government of Karnataka, to invest INR 2300 Crore |url=https://www.bengaluruairport.com/corporate/media/news-press-releases/air-india-and-tata-advanced-systems-limited-sign-mou-with-government-of-karnataka |work=Kempegowda International Airport Press Releases |date=19 February 2024 |access-date=19 February 2024 |language=en}} The MRO will be built on a {{convert|1524000|ft2|m2|order=flip|adj=on|}} parcel of land, and is expected to be operational by early 2026.{{cite news |title=Air India MRO in Bengaluru will be ready by early 2026, says CEO Wilson |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/air-india-mro-in-bengaluru-will-be-ready-by-early-2026-says-ceo-wilson/article68605881.ece |work=The Hindu |date=4 September 2024 |access-date=5 October 2024 |language=en}} ==== Central Kitchen ==== Food services provider [[SATS (company)|SATS]] set up their first central kitchen in India at the airport on 16 March 2024. A {{convert|150690|ft2|m2|order=flip|adj=on|}} facility, it was built with an investment of {{INRConvert|210|c}},{{cite web |date=26 July 2021 |title=SATS to establish Rs 210 cr central kitchen in India at Bengaluru airport |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/sats-to-establish-rs-210-cr-central-kitchen-in-india-at-bengaluru-airport-121072601232_1.html |work=Business Standard}} to cater to demand in the region. SATS already has a long-standing partnership with the airport, through its aviation catering associate TajSATS and ground handling associate AISATS. == Future plans == As part of the airport's masterplan, the completion of Terminal 2's Phase 2 will add an additional capacity of 20 million passengers per annum. There are also plans to build an [[People mover|APM]] (Automated People Mover) system that will seamlessly connect passengers between all terminals.{{cite news |last1=Philip |first1=Christin Mathew |date=30 November 2023 |title=Bengaluru airport likely to get automated people mover for seamless transfers between terminals |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/technology/bengaluru-airport-likely-to-get-automated-people-mover-for-seamless-transfers-between-terminals-11836171.html |work=Moneycontrol |access-date=9 January 2024}} The final phase of the master plan involves identifying a location for Terminal 3, though this is only expected in the late 2020s or early 2030s depending on passenger traffic. With Terminal 3, the airport is eyeing a capacity of 90-100 million passengers per annum.{{cite news |last1=Prasad |first1=Sanath |date=1 December 2023 |title=Bengaluru airport to roll out its master plan with renovation of T1, new place for T3 by 2030 |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/bangalore/bengaluru-airport-master-plan-renovation-9049746/ |work=The Indian Express |access-date=9 January 2024}}{{Cite web |title=With T3, Kempgowda airport eyeing a traffic of 90-100 million passengers |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/business/with-t3-kempgowda-airport-eyeing-a-traffic-of-90-100-mn-passengers-2791809 |access-date=29 December 2024 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}} In the interim, several infrastructure projects such as the construction of the Airport's Metro & Suburban Rail stations, as well as the Airport City, are planned.{{cite news |last1=Adnal |first1=Madhuri |date=25 December 2023 |title=Namma Metro Blue Line To KIA: Airport City Metro Station Construction Underway |url=https://www.oneindia.com/bengaluru/bengaluru-namma-metro-blue-line-to-kempegowda-international-airport-city-station-set-to-take-off-3712545.html |work=One India |access-date=9 January 2024}}{{cite news |title=Air India & Tata Advanced Systems to invest Rs 2,300 cr in Karnataka |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/air-india-tata-advanced-systems-to-invest-rs-2300-cr-in-karnataka/articleshow/107814246.cms |work=Economic Times |date=19 February 2024 |access-date=19 February 2024 |language=en}} As of August 2025, the airport's new Western cross-field taxiway is under construction, with civil works set to complete by H12026. Approximately {{convert|1.4|km|mi|order=flip|adj=on|}} in length, the 2 parallel taxiways will link the airport's 2 runways on the Western side of the airfield and will be able to accommodate Code-F aircraft. It is expected to be operational by December 2027.{{Cite web |title=K-RIDE sets ball rolling for suburban railway line from Majestic to Bengaluru airport |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/bengaluru/k-ride-sets-ball-rolling-for-suburban-railway-line-from-majestic-to-bengaluru-airport-3125386 |access-date=29 December 2024 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}} The plan to build a metro link between Bengaluru and its airport was revived in 2020, and is now under construction as part of the [[Blue Line (Namma Metro)|Blue Line]].{{cite news |first=S |last=Lalitha |work=[[The New Indian Express]] |date=12 October 2021 |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/bengaluru/2021/oct/12/bmrcl-will-spend-rs-800-cr-for-infra-for-2-metro-stations-to-airport-line-will-be-ready-by-dec-2024-2370708.html |title=BMRCL will spend Rs 800 crore for infra for two Metro stations to airport, line will be ready by December 2024 |access-date=8 November 2021}} The project will link [[Bengaluru]] with the airport under Phase 2 of the [[Namma Metro]] project, and is {{convert|58|km|mi|order=flip|adj=on|}} long. The line connects with the [[Red Line (Namma Metro)|Red]] & [[Orange Line (Namma Metro)|Orange]] Lines at [[Hebbala metro station|Hebbal]], the [[Pink Line (Namma Metro)|Pink]] Line at [[Nagawara metro station|Nagawara]], the [[Purple Line (Namma Metro)|Purple]] Line at [[Krishnarajapura metro station|K.R. Puram]] and the [[Yellow Line (Namma Metro)|Yellow]] Line at [[Central Silk Board metro station|Central Silk Board]], thus serving the entire city. The project is expected to open in 3 phases between June and December 2026.{{Cite news |date=15 March 2023 |title=𝐁𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐚𝐥𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐀𝐢𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭 𝐌𝐞𝐭𝐫𝐨 {{!}} Namma Metro Blue Line - Route, Map, & Cost |url=https://www.magicbricks.com/blog/bangalore-airport-metro/131352.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923215049/https://www.magicbricks.com/blog/bangalore-airport-metro/131352.html |archive-date=23 September 2024 |access-date=29 December 2024 |work=Magicbricks Blog |language=en |url-status=live }} There are 2 metro stations being built in the airport campus; 1 to serve the upcoming Airport City and the other one in the [[Transport hub|Multi Modal Transport Hub]] opposite [[Airport terminal|Terminal 2]].
